lines: The fortune is in the follow-up. Most people say yes after the second or third touch.
Rule one: always schedule the follow-up before you leave the conversation. Never leave it open.
Rule two: follow up when you say you will. Reliability builds the trust that closes.
When it's time to close, keep it simple. Ask: are you ready to get started today?
Then stay quiet, and let them answer. The first person to speak usually decides.
If yes, walk them through enrollment right then, step by step, so they never get stuck.
If not yet, that's fine — set the next follow-up and keep the door open warmly.
The moment someone joins, welcome them and start their first forty-eight hours immediately.
A good close isn't pressure — it's simply helping someone make a decision they already want.
Now they're on your team. Next, we learn to duplicate — to copy this with them. Let's go.
